GoCodingRules.Mission: Thin Go baseline inheriting coding-baseline. testing-baseline is selected independently for test artifacts, never pulled into production by this language rule. Grounding: Effective Go, Go Code Review Comments and go.dev/blog/go1.13-errors; formatter, error, visibility and naming idioms remain unchanged. Rules are agent instructions, not a second command pipeline. Only the configured selector/DAG determines authority gates; examples below are not defaults and must not be run as extra gates.

BeliefState.Axiom: Code is `gofmt`/`goimports`-clean — non-negotiable, zero config. `goimports` is preferred (it also groups and prunes imports). Tabs, tool-decided layout; there are no formatting debates in Go.

`error` is the last return value and every error is checked — never discarded with `_` unless the discard is deliberate and justified. Add context by wrapping with `fmt.Errorf("doing X: %w", err)` (`%w`, not `%v`, so callers can unwrap). Inspect with `errors.Is` / `errors.As`, not `==` or type assertions. Define a sentinel (`var ErrNotFound = errors.New(…)`) only for a condition callers actually branch on. Error strings are lowercase, no trailing punctuation.
Library code returns errors; it does not `panic` on ordinary or expected failures (bad input, missing file). `panic` is for programmer bugs and truly unrecoverable state only.

Capitalization is visibility — export only what callers need. No stutter: in package `env`, name it `env.Var`, not `env.EnvVar`; `New`/`Open`, not `NewEnv` inside `env`. Receiver names are short (1–2 letters) and consistent across a type's methods. Interfaces are small and `-er`-named; accept interfaces, return concrete structs.

AntiPattern.Bad: `_ = doThing()` or calling a function that returns `error` and not checking it.
AntiPattern.Instead: Check it: handle, or `return fmt.Errorf("…: %w", err)`. Discard only with a justifying comment.

AntiPattern.Bad: `panic("not found")` inside a reusable package for an expected condition.
AntiPattern.Instead: Return an `error` the caller can handle.

AntiPattern.Bad: `fmt.Errorf("read config: %v", err)` — `%v` flattens the error; `errors.Is/As` can no longer unwrap it.
`env.EnvVar`, `client.ClientConfig` — the package qualifier already carries the prefix.

Hook.Purpose: Code is gofmt-clean; formatting checks are read-only and use the configured exact scope.
Hook.Expected: No unformatted files in the configured required formatter report.

Hook.Purpose: Vet catches baseline bug classes when declared by the selected DAG.
Honor the project's declared linter (for example golangci-lint with govet, errcheck, staticcheck, ineffassign and unused). Do not silently skip a missing required linter.
Hook.Expected: A missing required executable is BLOCKED/ENV_FAIL, not PASS; this example installs no default gate.

Hook.Purpose: The behavior's tests pass under the project's configured test step.
Hook.Expected: The declared test step passes; production rule selection does not add a test phase.

GoCodingRules.RewardCriteria: ✅ `gofmt`/`goimports`-clean; any configured required vet step passes (for example `go vet ./...`). ✅ Every error checked; context added with `%w`; inspected via `errors.Is`/`As`. ✅ Library code returns errors, never panics on expected failures. ✅ No stutter; minimal exported surface; short consistent receiver names; small `-er` interfaces. ✅ When authoring tests with the declared stdlib `testing` runner: table-driven cases, `t.Run` and `t.Helper()` in helpers; no imposed third-party framework. ❌ An ignored/`_`-discarded error without justification. ❌ `panic` in library code for an expected failure. ❌ `%v` wrapping where `%w` is meant. ❌ Stutter naming (`env.EnvVar`). ❌ Speculatively-exported types/functions with no caller.
